props.html:
The following examples showcase the different features of the message group element.

The message group can be used to configure the way validation messages are displayed, depending on the referenced fields, groups or the type of rules.
Fields

children.text: In this example the message groups on the left side and right side are configured to display messages for specific fields. The messages for the configured field will be shown in the message group, while other errors will still be shown at the input.

props.html: In this example the message groups on the left side and right side are configured to display messages for specific fields. The messages for the configured field will be shown in the message group, while other errors will still be shown at the input.
Field: A
Field: B
Groups

children.text: In this example the message group on the left side is configured to display all messages of the whole document model group. In contrast, the message group on the right side will only handle messages related to a single field from this group.

props.html: In this example the message group on the left side is configured to display all messages of the whole document model group. In contrast, the message group on the right side will only handle messages related to a single field from this group.

Rules

children.text: In this example the message groups are configured to handle messages based on specific document model rules. On both sides errors for rules 1 and 2 will be triggered, when the precondition is set to true, failing field is set to a number != 42 and the document is validated.

Auto Collection

children.text: In this example the message groups have no fields, groups or rules set. On the left side, the automatic collection of document model elements from the container is enabled. So the message group automatically handles all elements that are referenced by an input in the container.
To demonstrate this, the inputs for A and B are nested in the message group, while the input for field C is not nested in the message group.

Formal Errors

children.text: In this example the message group on the left side is configured to ignore formal errors, so it only displays rule errors. The message group on the right side will display both formal errors and rule errors and additionally prefix formal errors with the label of the corresponding field.
the rule error will be triggered by setting the precondition to true

props.html:
In this example the message group on the left side is configured to ignore formal errors, so it only displays rule errors. The message group on the right side will display both formal errors and rule errors and additionally prefix formal errors with the label of the corresponding field.

Like above, the rule error will be triggered by setting the precondition to true, failing field to a value != 42 and validating the document.
Ignore Formal Errors
Prefix Formal Errors
Jump Links

children.text: Jump links will only be offered for elements that are contained in the message group. There will be one link to every related input in the order of these inputs. Links display the label of the individual input or the label from the Document Model if the input does not specify a label.
This example produces a rule error as above. On the left side, all related fields are contained in the message group, while the failing field is not contained in the message group on the right side.

Jump Links on Repeatable Inputs

children.text: When a message references multiple instances of the same field, jump links for every single instance should be displayed and lead the user to the correct repeatable instance.
To trigger an error over all repeatable instances, simply add some empty rows and validate the document.

Severity

children.text: The message group can handle messages of all severities. Messages are sorted by severity: ERROR -> WARNING -> INFO
To trigger all messages in this example, simply set the precondition to true and validate the document.
